GO-2026-5932 lives in the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package, which is frozen upstream with no fixed release. SpiceDB pulls golang.org/x/crypto for other subpackages but does not import the openpgp subtree into its shipped binaries; the scanner matches the module version against the advisory range regardless of reachability.

GO-2026-5932 is reported against golang.org/x/crypto@0.52.0 in the dockerize binary with vulnerable range '>=0' and no fix available. The advisory provides no details on the specific vulnerability, affected functions, or remediation path. The image already forces golang.org/x/crypto to 0.52.0 (the latest available at build time) to address prior CVE-2026-46598 and related advisories. Tracking upstream Go security advisories for a concrete fix or clarification on this UNSPECIFIED-severity finding.

GO-2026-5932 is scoped exclusively to the golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package and its subpackages (openpgp, openpgp/packet, openpgp/armor, openpgp/clearsign, openpgp/errors, openpgp/elgamal, openpgp/s2k), which are unmaintained with no fixed version. Neither prometheus nor promtool imports any openpgp subpackage: `go list -deps ./cmd/prometheus` and `./cmd/promtool` at v3.5.5 (x/crypto 0.54.0) and v3.12.0 (x/crypto 0.52.0) resolve only cryptobyte, chacha20poly1305, bcrypt, blowfish, pkcs12, and hkdf from golang.org/x/crypto. Go dead-code elimination means the vulnerable openpgp code is not compiled into the shipped binaries. Scout matches at the module level because the advisory records golang.org/x/crypto with no fixed version.

Neither prometheus nor promtool imports any openpgp subpackage: `go list -deps ./cmd/prometheus` and `./cmd/promtool` at v3.5.5 (x/crypto 0.54.0) and v3.12.0 (x/crypto 0.52.0) resolve only cryptobyte, chacha20poly1305, bcrypt, blowfish, pkcs12, and hkdf from golang.org/x/crypto. Go dead-code elimination means the vulnerable openpgp code is not compiled into the shipped binaries. Scout matches at the module level because the advisory records golang.org/x/crypto with no fixed version.

GO-2026-5932 covers the golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package, which upstream declares unmaintained and unsafe by design with no fixed version (all versions affected). govulncheck binary-mode symbol analysis of the shipped source-controller binary confirms vulnerable x/crypto/openpgp symbols are present and reachable (110 symbols, e.g. armor.Decode/armor.Encode), so this is not a false positive and cannot be excluded by a dependency bump. No patched x/crypto release exists and upstream fluxcd/source-controller has not migrated away from x/crypto/openpgp. Under investigation pending an upstream migration to a maintained OpenPGP implementation.
